recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future changes to allow plus signs on positiveInt or unsignedInt should be handled by a new work-group decision that explicitly reverses the FHIR-37368 computable-representation alignment.
issue_request: FHIR-12589 requested that integer and positiveInt regexes allow optional leading plus signs; it was Published/Persuasive for DSTU2 with resolution text 'allow +'.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by git-svn commit d142af1ffbabbd530f4804e65e3556a022ee9d32, matching Jira's svn @11056 comment, changing the old datatypes page to show plus-capable regexes for integer and positiveInt.
additional_context: Current datatype pages render regexes through macros backed by source/datatypes/primitives.xml. That source has integer and integer64 as [0]|[-+]?[1-9][0-9]*, while positiveInt is [1-9][0-9]* and unsignedInt is [0]|([1-9][0-9]*). Later Published FHIR-37368 explicitly resolved that the positiveInt page regex should match the computable/package representation, and commit 3ef54c37a52ed2d27ea04d457899585052cd4b1f changed the page from +?[1-9][0-9]* to [1-9][0-9]*. FHIR-16950 is range background only.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the integer portion of FHIR-12589 is already present, and adding plus support back to positiveInt would conflict with the later final FHIR-37368 decision.

related_jiras.note: Later Published datatypes issue corrected positiveInt from the old page-only +? regex to the computable/package representation without a leading plus. It is already represented on the combined branch.
Later Published datatypes issue clarified 32-bit ranges for integer, positiveInt, and unsignedInt; it does not change sign handling and is already represented on the combined branch.
